{

    "verdict": "Feasible as a conceptual controlled sensitivity experiment; clay content is a prescribable soil property in ELM and directly controls hydraulic parameters governing runoff/recharge partitioning.",
    "answerable": [
      "Direction and magnitude of runoff vs. recharge (drainage) partitioning as clay fraction increases from 5% to 55%",
      "Sensitivity of surface runoff (QOVER), subsurface drainage/recharge (QDRAI/QRECHARGE), and infiltration to clay content",
      "Changes in soil moisture profile and saturated hydraulic conductivity driven by clay-dependent pedotransfer functions"
    ],

      "Site-specific validation against observed runoff/recharge (no observations provided)",
      "Effects of covarying sand/organic matter or structure (held fixed by design)",

    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 6,
  "n_justification": "Six columns evenly span the requested clay range (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55%) at 10% intervals, sufficient to resolve a monotonic sensitivity curve while keeping the controlled experiment tractable. All other properties, location, and forcing are identical across columns so the only varying factor is clay content.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "clay05", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=5%, sand=45%, silt=50% (loam-like), identical across columns except clay"},
    {"id": "clay15", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=15%, sand=45%, silt=40%"},

    {"id": "clay45", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=45%, sand=45%, silt=10%"},
    {"id": "clay55", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=55%, sand=45%, silt=0%"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",

    "hist_variables": [
      "QRUNOFF",
      "QOVER",
      "QDRAI",
      "QRECHARGE",
      "QINFL",
      "QFLX_INFL",

  },

    "Ability to override PCT_CLAY/PCT_SAND in the ELM surface dataset per column",
    "Single-point/single-column ELM configuration (I-compset, e.g. I1PtClm or ELM_USRDAT single-column)",
    "GSWP3 or CRUNCEP atmospheric forcing for 1980-2018",
    "Accelerated-decomposition or hydrologic spinup capability prior to the transient run"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Clay is varied while sand is held at 45% and silt absorbs the remaining fraction; this keeps a single controlled axis (clay) though silt covaries by construction.",
    "All columns share identical PFT, atmospheric forcing, topographic slope, and initial conditions so runoff/recharge differences are attributable to clay-driven hydraulic parameters (via ELM pedotransfer functions).",

feasibility.verdict: Feasible as a conceptual controlled sensitivity experiment; clay content is a prescribable soil property in ELM and directly controls hydraulic parameters governing runoff/recharge partitioning.
answerable: Direction and magnitude of runoff vs. recharge (drainage) partitioning as clay fraction increases from 5% to 55%
Sensitivity of surface runoff (QOVER), subsurface drainage/recharge (QDRAI/QRECHARGE), and infiltration to clay content
Changes in soil moisture profile and saturated hydraulic conductivity driven by clay-dependent pedotransfer functions
not_answerable: Site-specific validation against observed runoff/recharge (no observations provided)
Effects of covarying sand/organic matter or structure (held fixed by design)
Sub-grid spatial heterogeneity or lateral flow beyond single-column vertical partitioning

parsed.n_justification: Six columns evenly span the requested clay range (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55%) at 10% intervals, sufficient to resolve a monotonic sensitivity curve while keeping the controlled experiment tractable. All other properties, location, and forcing are identical across columns so the only varying factor is clay content.

columns.soil_texture: clay=5%, sand=45%, silt=50% (loam-like), identical across columns except clay

requires_capabilities: Ability to override PCT_CLAY/PCT_SAND in the ELM surface dataset per column
Single-point/single-column ELM configuration (I-compset, e.g. I1PtClm or ELM_USRDAT single-column)
GSWP3 or CRUNCEP atmospheric forcing for 1980-2018
Accelerated-decomposition or hydrologic spinup capability prior to the transient run
assumptions: Clay is varied while sand is held at 45% and silt absorbs the remaining fraction; this keeps a single controlled axis (clay) though silt covaries by construction.

All columns share identical PFT, atmospheric forcing, topographic slope, and initial conditions so runoff/recharge differences are attributable to clay-driven hydraulic parameters (via ELM pedotransfer functions).
A 20-40 year accelerated spinup precedes the reported transient period to remove initial-condition bias in soil moisture and water table.
Recharge is diagnosed from bottom-layer drainage (QDRAI/QRECHARGE); surface runoff from QOVER; partitioning reported as long-term means.
Location chosen (Konza-region, Kansas) provides a temperate continental hydroclimate with meaningful runoff/recharge competition; results are conceptual, not a site calibration.
